territorial_scope.description: Sets general rules for AI systems developed, implemented or used in Brazil; no extraterritorial reach is stated in the text.

evidence.quote: for the development, implementation and responsible use of artificial intelligence (AI) systems in Brazil

agora_applications: Medicine, life sciences and public health
agora_harms: Violation of civil or human rights, including privacy

summary.short: Senate bill setting national rules for AI systems in Brazil. Grants affected persons rights to information, explanation and contestation; prohibits excessive-risk systems; imposes duties on high-risk systems, including impact assessments; sets civil liability and administrative sanctions; enters into force one year after publication.
summary.long: Federal Senate Bill No. 2338/2023 would set general national rules for the development, implementation and use of AI systems in Brazil, based on listed principles. It grants persons affected by AI systems rights to prior information, explanation of decisions, contestation and human review, and non-discrimination. Article 14 prohibits systems that use subliminal techniques, exploit vulnerabilities of specific groups, or are used by the public power for universal scoring. Article 15 restricts remote biometric identification in public spaces. Article 13 requires a preliminary risk assessment by the provider, and the competent authority updates the list of excessive and high-risk systems (Arts. 17-18). Providers and operators of high-risk systems must adopt governance measures, documentation, testing and algorithmic impact assessments (Arts. 20-26). Civil liability is objective for high- and excessive-risk systems and presumed-fault otherwise (Art. 27). The Executive designates a competent authority (Art. 32). Administrative sanctions include a fine limited to R$ 50,000,000.00 per infraction or 2% of revenue (Art. 36). Article 42 sets a text and data mining exception for listed bodies. The law would enter into force one year after publication (Art. 45).](Filler)

notes: Relations are stated only in this text; no registry IDs were available, so target_instrument_id is empty. The bill states no legal basis and amends, repeals or implements no existing act; it is a standalone bill with Art. 45 entry into force one year after publication. Items in the Justification (non-operative) are coded as cross-references and are marked as such. The bill's own history (introduction, Commission of Jurists, joint processing) is in the Justification only and is not coded as events here. Minor formatting artifacts in the text: duplicated list labels such as 'a) a)' in Arts. 20 IV, 24 § 1, 30 § 2 and 32 VI. Art. 13 § 3 uses 'upon prior notification' and Art. 22 refers to 'preliminary assessment' with no further detail; the operative rules depend on regulations not in this text.
